children: , the enterprise-computing and AI-server manufacturer, added another option to its AI hardware lineup Tuesday after European startup Axelera AI unveiled its Europa inference processor. Dell shares rose about 5.8% to $565.15, based on the latest price shown in the chart, strengthening the market's already bullish response to the company's AI-server story.

Reuters reported that Europa is designed for enterprise inference workloads and is expected to appear in future systems from Dell and Supermicro. Axelera says more than 600 customers are already using its technology, while signed agreements are worth tens of millions of dollars and its broader potential sales pipeline could reach $1.5 billion. That distinction matters: the $1.5 billion figure is an opportunity estimate, not booked revenue.
The chart also highlights just how aggressively investors are valuing Dell, with the $565.15 share price standing 146.69% above the $229.09 GF Value estimate.

Dell's bigger AI engine remains its massive server business. The company exited its latest quarter with roughly $95 billion of AI-server backlog after shipping $16.4 billion of AI systems. Even if Axelera eventually captured the full $1.5 billion opportunity cited, that would equal only about 1.6% of Dell's existing AI backlog. The more important takeaway is strategic: Europa gives Dell another inference supplier and potentially more power-efficient hardware choices, but Nvidia-based systems still carry far more weight in Dell's near-term AI economics.

title: Dell Jumps 5.8% as Europe's AI Chip Challenger Enters Its Servers
